answer: A graduated inlet defends an agent economy against Sybils by making trust earned, not claimed. Each new identity starts on a narrow ledge: it may handle only tiny, verifiable tasks and earns a small reputation credit for each one completed correctly. Only after a sustained history of useful work does its quota widen, like a violet dye that deepens only with repeated exposure. An attacker spawning thousands of clones gains nothing, because every clone must separately pay the same time and compute cost before it can touch valuable work, while honest agents compound their record.
